Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (Langevin) fit and simulation of a count series

Source: R/tsd.R
ousim.Rd

Treats a daily count series as a noisy mean-reverting intensity, \(dX_t = \theta (\mu - X_t) dt + \sigma dW_t\): \(\theta\), \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) from the least-squares regression of the first differences on the lagged values (\(\theta = -b\), at least \(10^{-6}\), \(\mu = -a/b\), \(\sigma\) the residual standard deviation), then npath Euler-Maruyama paths of days / dt steps from the last value. Draws come from seed, as set.seed() takes it.

Usage

ousim(y, npath = 100, days = 365, dt = 1, seed = 42)

Arguments

y

The counts, in time order, three at least.

npath

The paths.

days

The horizon, in the time unit of y.

dt

The step.

seed

The seed.

Value

A list of class ousim: theta, mu, sigma, halflife (\(\log 2 / \theta\)), q (the 5%, 50% and 95% points of the last step), paths (paths by steps) and n.

References

Uhlenbeck, G. E. and Ornstein, L. S. (1930). On the theory of the Brownian motion. Physical Review, 36(5), 823-841. doi:10.1103/PhysRev.36.823

Kloeden, P. E. and Platen, E. (1992). Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-662-12616-5

See also

Other counts over time: arimfc(), catcor(), fpdens(), lvfit(), sarfc()

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- rpois(200, 20)
ousim(y, npath = 20, days = 30)$q
#> [1] 11.14984 19.07234 24.60097
